candidate_relations.reason: Ocular melanosis does not represent the neurocutaneous vascular syndrome defined by the facial port-wine stains and associated ocular vascular abnormalities.

Phakomatosis pigmentovascularis requires a pigmentary nevus accompanying the capillary malformation; the described iris and fundus changes are ocular findings of Sturge-Weber syndrome rather than a documented cutaneous pigmentary nevus.
Ocular melanocytosis does not account for the bilateral trigeminal-distribution naevus flammeus and ocular vascular findings supporting Sturge-Weber syndrome.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Distinct congenital ocular melanocytic pigmentation disorder

candidate_relations.reason: The candidate exactly matches the reference diagnosis; absence of leptomeningeal malformation does not exclude an ocular-predominant Sturge-Weber presentation with facial capillary malformation, choroidal thickening, and glaucoma.
